definitions.explanation: The transition from wakefulness to sleep. Often used in medical or health-related contexts.

examples.japanese: {入眠|にゅうみん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{時間|じかん}がかかる→時間がかかる：26082_jikangakakaru⟧。
examples.english: It takes time to fall asleep.

examples.japanese: ⟦スマホ→スマホ：04721_sumaho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{入眠|にゅうみん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遅|おく}れ→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧やすい。
examples.english: Looking at your phone tends to delay sleep onset.

examples.japanese: ⟦{寝|ね}る→寝る：00470_neru⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦リラックス→リラックス：02531_rirakkusu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦スムーズ→スムーズ：11024_sumuuzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{入眠|にゅうみん}⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦ようになる→ようになる：28408_youninaru⟧。
examples.english: If you make a habit of relaxing before bed, you'll be able to fall asleep more smoothly.

notes:
Composed of {入|にゅう} (entering) + {眠|みん} (sleep). A somewhat formal or technical term commonly used in health articles, sleep research, and medical contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入眠|にゅうみん}⟦{障害|しょうがい}→障害：03228_shougai⟧ (difficulty falling asleep, a type of insomnia)
- {入眠|にゅうみん}⟦{儀式|ぎしき}→儀式：00071_gishiki⟧ (bedtime ritual)
- ⟦スムーズ→スムーズ：11024_sumuuzu⟧な{入眠|にゅうみん} (smooth sleep onset)
- {入眠|にゅうみん}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧ (time to fall asleep)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{寝|ね}つき→寝つき：08548_netsuki⟧ — falling asleep (more colloquial; ⟦{寝|ね}つき→寝つき：08548_netsuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧/⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧ is the common way to describe ease of falling asleep)
- ⟦{就寝|しゅうしん}→就寝：09947_shuushin⟧ — going to bed, retiring for the night (focuses on the act of going to bed, not the physiological transition)
- ⟦{睡眠|すいみん}→睡眠：03359_suimin⟧ — sleep (the state itself, not the process of falling asleep)
